title: Pathway Scorer and Backend Negotiator for OTEL Trace Routing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Implement a lightweight "pathway scorer" and a "backend negotiator" that decide, per-trace or per-span, the best destination backend(s) and any necessary format or envelope transformations. Goal is to reduce misrouted traces, improve backend acceptance rates, and enable preferential routing by customer tier and latency sensitivity.
background: We currently fan out OTLP envelopes to multiple backends with coarse tenant-level rules. As new backends (Tempo, Jaeger, vendor X) are onboarded with slightly different supported fields and quotas, we see partial rejections and increased error retries. A per-trace decision layer that understands path constraints and backend capabilities will reduce churn and avoid expensive retries.
goal: 1) Build a scorer that ranks candidate backends for a given trace based on schema compatibility, estimated size, sampling flag, customer tier, and recent backend health. 2) Build a negotiator that emits the minimal transformation (envelope, sampling hint, compression) to match the selected backend. 3) Make the component pluggable and observable with metrics and tracing hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Scorer returns deterministic ranking for test vectors covering legacy jaeger tags, large-span-envelopes (>1MB), and sparse sampled traces
Negotiator emits transform plans that include: envelope type, compression, sampling override, and field redaction rules
End-to-end integration test shows >=40% reduction in backend rejection errors for mixed backend clusters compared to baseline
New metrics exposed: pathway_scored_total, pathway_select_latency_ms, negotiation_transform_errors_total
Feature toggle present to enable/disable per-customer routing and canary rollout via console
technical_notes: Scorer inputs: tenant metadata, incoming OTLP headers, estimated proto size, root span attributes, recent backend health signals (from backend-health service)
Scoring factors (weightable): schema_compat (boolean), size_penalty (linear), sample_hint (enum), backend_latency_score, quota_headroom, tenant_priority
Negotiator responsibilities: choose envelope (otlp/protobuf vs jager/zipkin), apply required redactions, apply compression (gzip/snappy), attach tenant credentials or per-tenant routing token
Persistence: scoring rules stored in config service (json blobs) with versioning and rollout via config-leader; no per-trace DB writes
Runtime: implement as a lightweight service in edge path (written in Go), with sync cache of backend capability matrix
Fallback: if negotiator cannot produce compatible plan, fall back to current fanout route and emit negotiation_failure metric
implementation_plan: Design data model for backend capability matrix and scoring weights (doc link below)
Prototype scorer + negotiator as library, add unit tests for canonical vectors
Integrate library into otlp-ingest path behind feature flag; add end-to-end k8s canary
Instrument metrics and traces; wire to console dashboards (latency + error budget per backend)
Run 2-week canary with 5% of tenants, iterate on weights based on observed rejections
Gradually ramp to 100% and deprecate old coarse-routing code path
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring logic with table-driven cases
Integration tests: simulated backends with different acceptance rules (e.g., reject missing traceid, reject large envelopes)
Chaos test: simulate backend health flapping and verify scorer avoids unstable backends
Load test: ensure scorer+negotiator adds <1ms median overhead to ingest path at 10k TPS
Regression test suite: ensure existing tenant routing configs still honored when feature flag off
rollout_plan: Feature flag off by default; enable for internal orgs first
Canary: 5% of production tenants for 2 weeks, monitor negotiation_transform_errors_total and backend rejection rates
If metrics stable, ramp 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two release windows
Provide emergency kill switch in console and automated rollback playbook
